description: A lab member keeps rerunning similar experiments and needs a reliable way to remember which parameter changes were already tested, which failed, and which conditions still remain unexplored.

user_profile.context: The project is moving fast enough that failed branches are starting to repeat unintentionally
user_profile.communication_style: Technical and iterative, values a clean record of what not to retry

fact_sheet.fact: The official name of the research project is 'Project Chimera'.
Dr. Aris Thorne is the primary experimental researcher assigned to Project Chimera.
The primary objective of Project Chimera is to map cellular adhesion profiles under variable shear stress conditions.
All experimental parameters and results are mandated to be logged in the 'LabLogix' electronic lab notebook system.
The access URL for the LabLogix system is https://lablogix.bmil.institute.
Dr. Aris Thorne's username for LabLogix is 'athorne'.
The three substrate coatings being tested are Fibronectin (FN), Collagen Type I (C1), and Laminin (LN).
The specific shear stress levels being investigated are 5, 10, 15, and 20 dyn/cm².
The two cell types used in the assays are HUVEC-C (Lot #H4882-03B) and MSC-TERT (Lot #M9101-11A).
Experiment ID 'EXP-CHM-087', run on 2023-10-11, failed due to complete HUVEC-C cell detachment on a Fibronectin substrate at 20 dyn/cm².
The failure of EXP-CHM-087 was tagged in LabLogix with '#detachment_failure' to prevent re-running this condition.
Experiment ID 'EXP-CHM-102', run on 2023-10-18, showed optimal MSC-TERT adhesion on a Collagen Type I substrate at 5 dyn/cm² after a 24-hour incubation.
A search in LabLogix on 2023-11-01 confirms that the combination of Laminin substrate with MSC-TERT cells at any shear stress level remains unexplored.
As of 2023-11-01, no experiments have been conducted using a 48-hour incubation period for any parameter set.
The standard operating procedure for the 'Cellular Adhesion Assay under Shear Stress' is documented in file CAA-SOP-004b.pdf.
The CAA-SOP-004b.pdf is stored on the lab server at '//bmil-server/protocols/active/CAA-SOP-004b.pdf'.
Raw image files must follow the naming convention: YYYYMMDD_EXP-ID_CellType-Substrate-Shear_Replicate#.tiff.
The analysis scripts for Project Chimera are version-controlled in a Git repository at 'git@git.bmil.institute:chimera/analysis.git'.
The Ibidi Pump System 3, serial number IB-PS3-9440B, is the designated equipment for applying shear stress.
The Ibidi Pump System 3 is permanently located at the workstation on Wet Lab Bench 4.
The Principal Investigator overseeing Project Chimera is Dr. Lena Petrova.
Kenji Tanaka is the Lab Manager and the point of contact for ordering consumables; his email is ktanaka@bmil.institute.
For IT support specifically related to the LabLogix system, the designated contact email is support-lablogix@bmil.institute.
The dedicated Slack channel for all informal, daily discussions related to Project Chimera is #proj-chimera.
The weekly Project Chimera progress meeting is held every Friday at 10:00 AM Eastern Time via Zoom link https://bmil.zoom.us/j/9876543210.
The current SOP to consult for the Cellular Adhesion Assay under Shear Stress is `CAA-SOP-004b.pdf`, stored at `//bmil-server/protocols/active/CAA-SOP-004b.pdf`.
For Project Chimera, raw image files must be named using the pattern `YYYYMMDD_EXP-ID_CellType-Substrate-Shear_Replicate#.tiff`.
